description: KLR tranche 2 — Demazure-Lusztig variant of Composite 1 preflight RUN. Fourth (last) preflight in the cont. 9 menu series after Composite 4 (magnitude), Composite 1 standard (sign), Composite 3 Type-B folded (sign). Computes the Lusztig-dual Demazure character at sl_3 / ω_1 / ℓ=2 using D_w^{dual}(q) = q^{ht}·D_w(q^{-1}), shows it is positive at q > 0 (Laurent polynomial with non-negative coefficients in the natural bar-pairing). Combined with (q;q)_2 > 0 at q > 1, [u²]F > 0 — sign-incompatible with c_2 = -1. NATURAL Lusztig variants (dual, T_i-action) all inherit this positivity. Exotic signed variants (Lusztig-Yun-Zhu, twisted) UNTESTED and require a separate scope. Honest verdict: NARROWS cont. 9 Option C to exotic-signed variants only.

data.interpretation: The Lusztig involution on the Hecke algebra produces canonical bases that are bar-INVARIANT but POSITIVE at q > 0 (Lusztig's canonical basis is a positive integral basis; this is Lusztig 1990's positivity theorem for type A). So the natural Demazure-Lusztig characters inherit positivity from the unsigned Demazure crystal model. The sign refutation of Composite 1 standard transfers to Composite 1 Lusztig-dual without modification. Exotic signed conventions (Lusztig-Yun-Zhu Whittaker, twisted T_i with sign-flipping) exist mathematically but are not in this corpus's natural categorical framework — they would require an explicit convention specification before the preflight pattern applies. **Net for the KLR program**: the natural reading of cont. 9 Option C is fully refuted (standard + dual variants); the residual escape route is exotic-signed Lusztig variants, which are a separate research-grade scope item rather than a build-cost-saving preflight.
